verdict.rationale: Sill streams a single Mac window, not only a mirror of the whole desktop. Its off-by-default virtual display moves that window onto a separate display on the Mac, so the iPad effectively shows content living on its own display. However, nothing documents the device acting as a general extended desktop that you can drag windows onto and arrange alongside the main screen. Missing for 10: documented extended-desktop/second-monitor mode with free window placement, display arrangement, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, a tablet or spare device works as an additional display that extends the desktop, not only a mirror of it

citations.quote: The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.
Sill shows a window from your Mac, or its whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad
